GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2022-06-16T09:22:50Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Mismatch between CSDiagnostic line number in message and location
Description: I am having a problem evaluating compilation errors generated during CSharpCompilation.Emit.

I am using roslyn to generate CS code with #line directives containing unique ids of source objects that were used to generate the source following each #line directive as line number.

Now when there is an error during compilation (i.e. incompatible argument types), I would like to retrieve the unique id of my source object. 

```
var result = compilation.Emit(
                    peStream: stream
                    , pdbStream: symbolsStream
                    , embeddedTexts: embeddedTexts
                    , options: emitOptions);

                messages = result.Diagnostics
                    .Where(diagnostic => diagnostic.Severity == DiagnosticSeverity.Error)
                    .Select(diagnostic =>
                    {
                        var location = diagnostic.Location.GetMappedLineSpan();
                        var message = diagnostic.GetMessage(); // message contains the correct "line number" (Id)
                        // message is "generated.cs(640,1): error CS1503: ... and so on"
                        return (NetworkError)new UnknownNetworkError(
                            nodeId: location.StartLinePosition.Line,  // Problem here! Line should be 640, but is 639.
                            errorMessage: message);
                    })
                    .ToList();
```

The generated code looks like that (method names changed):
```
#line 640
            outputRoot.MethodExpectingFoo(child:

#line 576
            SomeStaticClass.StaticMethodReturningBar()

#line 640
);
```

So can anyone tell me where I can find the actual line number as it is mentioned inside the error message? I am not sure if this is an error or if I am looking in the wrong location (pun intended).

Thank you!
